transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-05 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Aurora CTO), Samir Khan (Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Eng Manager)

Summary (auto):
Aurora AI is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for dev/prod non-sensitive traffic and Dedicated or Private (VPC) for PII-sensitive inference. Key integration questions: SDK support (Python/TS), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy architecture for routing to Hosted vs Dedicated, rate limits/quotas and burst handling, and observability hooks (trace ids, token-level cost). Next steps: Redwood to share integration examples and pricing, Aurora to share prompt set and traffic profile, schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics discussed: SDKs (python/js), LangChain & LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy routing, rate limits and quotas, observability/tracing hooks, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC), performance benchmarks and fallback policies.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the A E on this account, with Ravi our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Elena Morales: Good thanks, thanks for doing this. Quick note, timezone stuff - so we have about an hour.
[00:09] Ravi Patel: great, we'll keep it tight. At a high level we want to understand your integration goals, current infra, and any blockers for Dedicated or Private.
[00:15] Samir Khan: Sure. Our main use case is real-time summarization and conversational support inside Aurora's product; some queries contain user identifiers and PII so we need a path to isolate that traffic. We're evaluating hosted for general traffic, but Dedicated/VPC for PII.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: We care about latency - 95th under 150ms for short prompts - and cost per 1k tokens. Also need observability hooks so our SRE can attribute cost/latency per route.
[00:39] Maya Chen: totally. A few quick Qs - what's your current stack for orchestration and vector stores? Are you using LangChain or LlamaIndex today?
[00:46] Samir Khan: We're prototyping with LangChain - a mixture of chain-of-thought and retrieval-augmented prompts. We also have an internal vector db but we're ok with offloading embeddings to Redwood if it helps.
[00:55] Ravi Patel: good to know. On SDKs, we have first-class Python and Typescript SDKs and examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. We also provide a lightweight gateway pattern - either you call Redwood direct from service code, or you run a proxy/gateway that routes requests to Hosted vs Dedicated based on headers or token-scopes.
[01:10] Elena Morales: Can you elaborate on the gateway? We have strict egress policies and would prefer a single outbound to centralize firewall rules.
[01:16] Ravi Patel: yeah, that's common. Two patterns: 1) client-side routing - app decides target; 2) centralized proxy - a small service you run in your VPC that inspects the request metadata and forwards to Redwood's endpoints. The proxy supports persistent connections and can multiplex to reduce TLS overhead. We have a sample Go/Node proxy in our github repo.
[01:33] Samir Khan: What about auth between proxy and Redwood - service keys or mTLS?
[01:36] Maya Chen: We support API keys, and for Dedicated/Private we additionally support mTLS and token exchange via your IdP. For Private on-prem we can negotiate direct peering or private link.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: Observability - can we get trace ids propagated? We instrument everything with OpenTelemetry.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can accept X-Trace-Id headers and emit them through our logs and trace collection. We also include token-level breakdowns in the Console so you can see cost per call, latency per route, and model version. We can stream logs to your Splunk/Datadog via SIEM integration or S3 export.
[02:05] Elena Morales: Are there rate limits or quotas? We have bursty traffic during promotions.
[02:09] Ravi Patel: For Hosted API there are account-level quotas and per-key rate limits; for Dedicated you get predictable throughput tied to your reserved capacity - you can define soft and hard quotas and autoscale policies for burst. We also provide a throttling response header so your gateway can backoff before hitting hard limits.
[02:26] Samir Khan: Any throttling behavior - do you queue? drop? how is fairness enforced?
[02:30] Ravi Patel: We do a combination: short-term queuing with a best-effort routing; if capacity is saturated, we have graceful fallback policies - e.g., route to a smaller model or to Hosted spare capacity if allowed by your policy. You can define priorities per route.
[02:42] Maya Chen: also worth calling out KV cache/prefix caching - for chat workloads we can significantly reduce cost and latency if your app can reuse cached prefixes.
[02:50] Samir Khan: interesting. Is that automatic or do we have to implement?
[02:53] Ravi Patel: mostly automatic: the runtime supports KV cache and we expose controls - TTLs, cache keys, and you can configure whether to persist between sessions. For privacy-sensitive flows we can disable persistence.
[03:02] Lena Ortiz: Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO, KMS integration - do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:07] Maya Chen: yes for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. We also provide audit logs, RBAC in Console, and SSO (SAML/OIDC). We'll send our security pack after the call.
[03:16] Elena Morales: Good. Can you share an example of the LangChain connector code? I want to see how much glue code we need.
[03:20] Ravi Patel: Sure - we have a LangChain adapter that plugs into LLMChain with two lines of code; same for LlamaIndex where we provide a simple loader. I'll share a repo link and a small Jupyter notebook that runs a 1000-query micro-benchmark against Hosted and Dedicated.
[03:35] Samir Khan: How do you handle tool-calling / function calls in streaming scenarios? We need structured outputs for downstream systems.
[03:41] Ravi Patel: We support function/tool calling in streaming mode and can send partial tokens as they are generated. The SDK surfaces structured JSON events so you can route them into your processing pipeline. There are examples in the client libs.
[03:50] Maya Chen: any questions on pricing model - utility (per token) vs reserved capacity?
[03:54] Elena Morales: We're trying to compare blended cost for 50M tokens/month: mostly short prompts, high QPS. We also need to account for egress and SLA for Dedicated.
[04:03] Maya Chen: we'll run an apples-to-apples. For Dedicated we can model cost per reserved GPU-hour plus a small per-token charge for wrappers. For Hosted we have per-token pricing and volume tiers. I'll include a sample estimate in the pricing doc.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: For pilot, can we get a pinned model version and a canary rollout option? We want to test model changes without impacting prod.
[04:19] Ravi Patel: yes - we support pinning model versions and rollout strategies: canary %, A/B weights, and automatic fallback to a stable variant on errors.
[04:27] Samir Khan: important: our product team will want to use LlamaIndex for retrieval augmented generation. Are there examples of hooking up your embedding endpoint with LlamaIndex?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: yes - we provide an embeddings client that LlamaIndex can call; plus we have a small connector that converts Redwood embedding responses into the index format. I'll attach code.
[04:43] Elena Morales: Perf: do you have benchmarks for 95th latency on NVidia A100 vs H100? We have preferences depending on model family.
[04:49] Ravi Patel: we publish verified perf profiles for common models and hardware in our model catalog; we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet with tail latencies. For custom models we can run a short benchmark during the pilot.
[04:58] Maya Chen: any blockers on your side for a pilot?
[05:02] Samir Khan: we need to validate security, and we need examples for LangChain/LlamaIndex integration. Also want to confirm gateway pattern and the burden to run it.
[05:09] Maya Chen: understood. Action items summarized at the end. We'll send the security pack, integration samples, and pricing.
[05:15] Elena Morales: timeline - CTO org wants a pilot in mid-August, ideally the week of 8/17. That works for us.
[05:22] Maya Chen: great, we'll target that.
[05:25] Ravi Patel: i'll post the repo links, the benchmark notebook, and a small proxy example.
[05:30] Lena Ortiz: quick question - what logging granularity do you support? We need per-request token counts and model version.
[05:35] Ravi Patel: per-request token counts, model id, customer route, and X-Trace-Id; you can consume via streaming logs or S3 export. Data retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[05:44] Samir Khan: How do you handle data residency - some EU customers require data to stay in-region.
[05:49] Maya Chen: Hosted supports region selection and we have Private deployments for strict residency. For Dedicated we can provision in-region capacity.
[05:55] Elena Morales: ok that covers most. Thanks.
[05:58] Maya Chen: thanks all. We'll follow up with docs and scheduling.
